name: Sprouted Moong Chaat Bowl
tagline: Regular chaat swaps fried sev/puri for sprouted moong + roasted peanuts — same tang, way more protein and fiber
healthySwap: Sprouted moong + roasted peanuts instead of fried sev/puri

prepAhead.task: Sprout the moong (soak 8 hrs, drain, leave covered at room temp, rinsing once)
Dice onion, tomato, and cucumber and refrigerate

steps: If not pre-sprouted, soak moong overnight and let it sprout for 1-2 days (see prep-ahead).
In a bowl, combine sprouted moong, potato, onion, tomato, and cucumber.
Add roasted peanuts, chaat masala, and salt.
Squeeze lemon juice over the mix and toss well.
Garnish with coriander and serve immediately (don't dress ahead of time or it goes soggy).

name: Paneer Tikka Salad
tagline: Restaurant tikka minus the heavy oil — air-fried instead of pan-fried in ghee, served over greens instead of naan
healthySwap: Air-fried instead of pan-fried in ghee, served over greens instead of naan

prepAhead.task: Wash and store greens in an airtight container

steps: Mix hung curd, tikka masala, ginger-garlic paste, and a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Add paneer, bell pepper, and onion cubes; coat well. Marinate at least 30 min (ideally overnight).
Thread onto skewers, or place directly in the air-fryer basket lightly greased with the oil.
Air-fry at 200°C for 12-15 minutes, turning halfway, until edges char slightly.
Plate the greens, top with the air-fried paneer and peppers.
Drizzle mint chutney over the top and serve warm.

name: Chicken Tikka Protein Salad
tagline: Same tikka marinade logic with chicken breast — high protein, low effort after a long commute
healthySwap: Air-fried chicken breast tikka instead of fried/pan-cooked
steps: Combine hung curd, tikka masala, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and salt.
Add chicken cubes, coat thoroughly, and marinate at least 2 hours (ideally overnight, in the fridge).
Air-fry at 200°C for 15-18 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until cooked through (internal temp 75°C).
Toss greens, cucumber, and onion in a bowl.
Top with the air-fried chicken tikka pieces.
Serve with mint-yogurt dip on the side.

name: Beetroot Kathi Roll (Paneer Bhurji)
tagline: Beetroot-kneaded roti instead of plain maida roti — natural color, extra fiber, no maida
healthySwap: Beetroot-kneaded whole wheat roti instead of plain maida roti

ingredients.name: Beetroot
ingredients.unit: small, boiled and pureed (~2 tbsp puree), for the roti

prepAhead.task: Knead the beetroot dough and refrigerate

steps: Knead whole wheat flour with beetroot puree, a pinch of salt, and water as needed into a soft dough. Rest 15 min.
Roll into 2 thin rotis and cook on a hot tawa until light brown spots appear on both sides.
Heat oil in a pan, sauté onions until translucent, add capsicum and tomato, cook 3-4 min.
Add crumbled paneer and roll masala, mix well, cook 3-4 min until combined.
Spoon the bhurji filling onto each roti, roll tightly, and serve warm.

name: Egg Bhurji Roll, Spinach Roti
tagline: Spinach-pureed roti sneaks in greens, wrapped around a light egg bhurji
healthySwap: Spinach-pureed whole wheat roti sneaks in greens

ingredients.name: Spinach
ingredients.unit: cup, blanched and pureed, for the roti

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.unit: small, finely chopped, for the filling

prepAhead.task: Make the spinach roti dough and refrigerate

steps: Knead flour with spinach puree and a pinch of salt into a soft dough. Rest 15 min, roll into 2 rotis, and cook on a tawa.
Heat oil in a pan, sauté onion and green chili until soft.
Add turmeric and beaten eggs, scramble on medium heat until just cooked.
Spoon the egg bhurji onto each roti, roll, and serve warm.

name: Chana Patty Roll (Chickpea Burger Filling as a Roll)
tagline: The chickpea-patty-instead-of-meat trick, wrapped in a roti instead of a bun
healthySwap: Chickpea patty instead of meat, wrapped in a roti instead of a bun

prepAhead.task: Shape and refrigerate patties, or batch-make and freeze

steps: Mash chickpeas roughly (leave some texture), mix with ground oats, onion, garlic, cumin, chili powder, and salt.
Shape into 4 small patties. Refrigerate 20 min to firm up.
Air-fry at 190°C for 12-15 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and firm.
Warm the rotis, spread mint chutney, place patties in each, top with sliced onion, and roll.

name: Masala Millet Khichdi
tagline: Millet instead of white rice — lower GI, more fiber, same comfort-food feel
steps: Wash and soak millet and moong dal together for at least 30 min (overnight is better).
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker or pot, add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped vegetables, sauté 2 min.
Add drained millet-dal mix, turmeric, salt, and water.
Pressure cook for 3-4 whistles (or simmer covered for 20-25 min, stirring occasionally, until soft).
Serve hot, with a small drizzle of ghee on top if desired.

name: Egg Fried Brown Rice, Indian-Spiced
tagline: Brown rice instead of white, extra egg-to-rice ratio for protein, minimal oil
healthySwap: Brown rice instead of white, extra egg for protein, minimal oil
steps: Heat oil in a wok or wide pan on high heat.
Add spring onion whites and carrot, stir-fry 2 min.
Push veggies to one side, pour beaten egg into the empty space, scramble until just set.
Add the chilled brown rice, breaking up any clumps.
Add soy sauce and garam masala, toss everything together on high heat for 3-4 min.
Garnish with spring onion greens and serve hot.

name: Chicken Keema Rice, One-Pot
tagline: Lean chicken keema instead of mutton, brown rice instead of white, cooked together for minimal cleanup
healthySwap: Lean chicken keema instead of mutton, brown rice instead of white

prepAhead.task: Marinate keema with ginger-garlic paste and garam masala

steps: Heat oil in a pressure cooker or pot, sauté onions until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 min, then add tomato and cook until soft.
Add chicken keema, garam masala, and salt; cook until the keema changes color (5-6 min).
Add washed brown rice, peas, and water.
Pressure cook for 3-4 whistles, or simmer covered for 25-30 min until rice is tender.
Rest 5 min before serving.

name: Tandoori Chicken Marinade
tagline: Protein-prep focused marinade, reusable across the week
healthySwap: Air-fried or oven-roasted instead of deep-fried, minimal oil marinade

prepAhead.task: Marinate, or batch-marinate and freeze in portions

steps: Make small cuts in the chicken pieces to let the marinade penetrate.
Mix curd, ginger-garlic paste, tandoori masala, lemon juice, oil, chili powder, and salt into a smooth marinade.
Coat the chicken thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate at least 4 hours (overnight is best).
Air-fry at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until charred at the edges and cooked through — OR oven-roast at 220°C for 20-25 min.
Rest 5 min before serving.

name: Soya Chaap Marinade
tagline: Protein-prep focused marinade, reusable across the week
healthySwap: Air-fried or pan-seared with minimal oil instead of deep-fried

prepAhead.task: Marinate; soya chaap also freezes well pre-marinated

steps: If using stick chaap, slice into bite-size pieces.
Mix curd, ginger-garlic paste, chaap masala, kasuri methi, oil, and salt into a marinade.
Coat chaap pieces well, refrigerate at least 2 hours (overnight for best flavor).
Air-fry at 190°C for 12-15 min, turning halfway — OR pan-sear on a hot tawa, 8-10 min, turning occasionally, until charred spots form.

name: Veggie-Loaded Whole Wheat Pasta
tagline: Whole wheat pasta instead of refined, sauce bulked with pureed vegetables instead of heavy cream
healthySwap: Whole wheat pasta and vegetable-bulked sauce instead of refined pasta and heavy cream
steps: Boil pasta in salted water per package instructions until al dente. Reserve 2 tbsp pasta water, then drain.
Heat olive oil in a pan, sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add tomato puree, cook 5-6 min until it thickens slightly.
Add bell pepper and zucchini, cook 4-5 min until just tender.
Add dried herbs, salt, and pepper. Stir in the reserved pasta water if the sauce is too thick.
Toss the cooked pasta into the sauce and mix well. Serve hot.

name: Schezwan Egg Noodles, Lighter Version
tagline: Whole wheat noodles, less oil than street-style, extra egg and veg for protein/fiber
healthySwap: Whole wheat noodles and less oil than street-style, extra egg and veg
steps: Boil noodles per package instructions until just done, drain, and toss with a few drops of oil to prevent sticking.
Heat oil in a wok, scramble the egg lightly, remove and set aside.
In the same wok, stir-fry cabbage and carrot on high heat for 2-3 min (keep it crunchy).
Add boiled noodles, schezwan sauce, and the scrambled egg back in. Toss everything together for 2 min.
Garnish with spring onion and serve hot.

name: Sattu Protein Ladoo
tagline: Roasted channa sattu + jaggery instead of sugar — batch-friendly, no refined sugar
healthySwap: Roasted channa sattu + jaggery instead of refined sugar

prepAhead.storesFor: ~5 days at room temp, ~2 weeks refrigerated

steps: Dry-roast the sattu lightly for 2-3 min if not already roasted. Let cool.
Mix sattu, grated jaggery, and cardamom powder in a large bowl.
Add melted ghee gradually, mixing with your hands until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Roll into 12 ladoos (about 20g each).
Store in an airtight container.

name: Roasted Makhana Chaat
tagline: Fox nuts roasted in minimal ghee with chaat masala instead of fried namkeen
healthySwap: Fox nuts roasted in minimal ghee instead of fried namkeen
steps: Heat ghee in a pan on low-medium heat.
Add makhana and roast, stirring continuously, for 8-10 min until crisp (should sound hollow when tapped).
Add turmeric, chaat masala, and salt, tossing to coat evenly.
Mix in roasted peanuts, let cool completely.
Store in an airtight container once fully cooled (keeps them crisp).

name: Ragi Chocolate Energy Bites
tagline: Ragi flour + dates + cocoa instead of maida + refined sugar — doubles as a pre-workout bite
healthySwap: Ragi flour + dates + cocoa instead of maida + refined sugar
steps: Dry-roast ragi flour on low heat for 3-4 min until fragrant. Let cool.
Soak dates in warm water for 10 min if dry/hard, then drain.
Blend dates, cocoa powder, and peanut butter into a thick paste.
Mix in roasted ragi flour and chia seeds until well combined and moldable.
Roll into 14 small balls (~15g each).
Refrigerate at least 30 min to firm up before serving.
